keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: Niches to search for — `med spa`, `realtor`, `wedding photographer`. Each keyword is searched separately.

location.title: Location
location.description: Optional. Added to every query as a phrase, so it matches profiles whose bio names the place — `Austin TX`, `Scottsdale`.

emailDomains.title: E-mail domains
emailDomains.description: Searched one at a time, and results are filtered to them. Naming the domain in the query is what makes the search return profiles that publish an address at all. Leave empty for the built-in set: gmail, yahoo, hotmail, outlook, icloud, aol.

site.title: Site
site.description: The profile host to restrict the search to. `tiktok.com` and `twitter.com` work the same way.

engine.title: Search engine
engine.description:
**DuckDuckGo** has a plain HTML endpoint with no CAPTCHA — the only one that works from a script for free. **Google** has a far better `site:` index but blocks datacenter IPs within a few queries; pick it only with residential proxies.

For Google without paying for anything, run the same searches from the browser extension instead: it searches from your own logged-in session and is never challenged.
enumTitles: Google — better index, needs residential proxies

maxEmails.title: Max addresses
maxEmails.description: Stops once this many profiles carry an address. `0` means no limit.

requireEmail.title: Only keep profiles with an address
requireEmail.description: A profile whose snippet holds no address is of little use here — the whole point is that the address is already in the search result.

oneRowPerEmail.title: One row per address
oneRowPerEmail.description: A profile with two addresses becomes two rows. Matches the shape the commercial actors emit.

dropUndeliverable.title: Drop addresses whose domain has no mail server

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Not needed for DuckDuckGo. Close to mandatory for Google.
